Diastereoselective and Enantioselective Hydrophosphinylations of
Conjugated Enynes, Allenes and Dienes via Synergistic Pd/Co
Catalysis
Ming-Qiao Tang, Zi-Jiang Yang, Ai-Jun Han, and Zhi-Tao He*
Abstract: Different from the reported work focusing on
the construction of single P- or C-stereocenter via
hydrophosphinylation of unsaturated carbon bonds, the
highly diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphiny-
lation reaction of allenes, conjugated enynes and 1,3-
dienes is achieved via a designed Pd/Co dual catalysis
and newly modified masked phosphinylating reagent. A
series of allyl motifs bearing both a tertiary C- and
P-stereocenter are prepared in generally good yields,
>20: 1 dr, >20: 1 rr and 99% ee. The unprecedented
diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinylation of
1,3-enynes is established to generate skeletons contain-
ing both a P-stereocenter and a nonadjacent chiral axis.
The first stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation reaction
is also developed to achieve all four P-containing stereo-
isomers. The present protocol features the use of only
3-minutes reaction time and 0.1 % catalyst, and with the
observation of up to 730 TON. A set of mechanistic
studies reveal the necessity and roles of two metal
catalysts and corroborate the designed synergistic proc-
ess.

ways such as 1,4-conjugate addition, allylic substitution,

asymmetric hydrophosphinylation and hydrophosphination
of unsaturated carbon-carbon bonds have emerged as a
valuable and convenient route to construct these
skeletons.<sup>[3–9]</sup> For example, in 2018, Dong reported the first

vated 1,3-dienes.<sup>[4b]</sup> Wang and Li extended hydrophosphina-
tion and hydrophosphinylation to the use of allenes with

sively on the construction of P- or C-stereocenter and fail to
provide high stereocontrol on both of them simultaneously
(Scheme 1a). A few prior works tried to establish the related
diastereoselective processes but generally furnished 1: 1
diastereoselectivity for the transformations.<sup>[4h,l,5b,f,8]</sup> Only an
elegant work by Li and co-workers describes diastereoselec-
tive access to phosphine-functionalized olefins via Pd-
catalyzed hydrophosphination of alkynes.<sup>[4i]</sup> Thus, the route

related hydrophosphinylation and hydrophosphination proc-
esses remain undeveloped, neither enantioselectively nor
diastereoselectively.

Herein, we describe our endeavors to establish three
types of diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinyla-
tion transformations via a synergistic Pd/Co catalysis
(Scheme 1c). With allene and newly modified masked P(V)
reagent as the substrates, the hydrophosphinylation can be
realized to generate skeletons bearing both a P- and
C-stereocenter. The hydrophosphinylation of 1,3-enynes is

and a chiral axis. This protocol is further applied to the

conjugated diene. In addition, a stereodivergent protocol is
described to access all of the stereoisomers of the con-
structed P-containing units.
Results and Discussion
With this design in mind, aryloxyallene 1a and pyridyl
phosphine oxide 2a-1 were selected as the electrophile and
nucleophile, respectively (Table 1). When BINAP L5 was
selected as the chiral ligand for Pd catalyst, a set of chiral
ligands for Co metal was evaluated first. With Boxmi ligand
L1 used,<sup>[19]</sup> the synergistic catalysis occurred and provided
3a in 36% yield and 60 % ee but with 1.4: 1 dr (entry 1).
When a similar ligand L2 was used instead, both the
reactivity and stereocontrol were increased obviously. In
this case, 77% yield, 4.5:1 dr and 79 % ee for product 3 a
were observed (entry 2). Other chiral ligands did not show
better stereocontrol for the hydrofunctionalization process
(see Supporting Information for details). Next, a group of
chiral ligands instead of L5 for Pd metal was checked
(entries 3–9). Among them, L10 exhibited the optimal
results, furnishing 3a in 75 % yield, 11: 1 dr and 96% ee. A
series of other condition evaluations including different
bases and solvents were conducted. The corresponding
results were summarized in the Supporting Information but
all failed to provide superior effects.

phosphonate as the masked phosphonating reagent could
prevent catalyst deactivation and presumably have a positive
influence on reactivity and selectivity.<sup>[20]</sup> Several modified

the reaction of 2a-1 and ketones. We found that these new
phosphonating reagents are actually much easier to be
prepared and purified than that for 2a-1. With 2 a used

ity and enantioselectivity of 3 a were elevated (from 11 : 1 to
>20 :1 dr and 96 % to 97 % ee). Similarly, 2a-2 and 2a-3 as

with slightly decreased yields for 3a (entries 11–12). When
the reaction temperature was lowered to room temperature,

3a decreased heavily (entry 14). This fact suggested the

Inspired by the high efficiency of the present protocol,
we guessed that a low catalyst loading might still provide
comparable reactivity. Indeed, when 0.05 % [Pd(allyl)Cl]
was adopted under standard conditions, the hydrofunction-

and 97% ee. The corresponding catalyst turnover number
(TON) was as high as 720. To the best of our knowledge, no
previous work was reported with such a high efficiency for
asymmetric hydrofunctionalizations of unsaturated carbon-
carbon bonds. Both the short reaction time and low catalyst
loading showcase the power of this method.

Conclusion
Three protocols have been described for the highly diaster-
eo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinylation of allenes,
1,3-enynes and conjugated dienes via Pd/Co dual catalysis.
Two types of motifs bearing both a P- and C-stereocenter or
both a P-stereocenter and chiral axis are prepared in good
yields and with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantiose-
lectivities. A modified P(V) compound as a masked
unsymmetric phosphinylating reagent is critical to the
achievement of high stereoselectivities for the transforma-
tion. The unreported stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation
reaction is also realized to access all four stereoisomers of
phosphinylated allenes. In addition, the reaction features a
very short reaction time and low catalyst loading and can be
run on gram-scale, all of which make this protocol powerful
and practically valuable. Preliminary mechanistic experi-
ments elucidate the role of two catalysts and suggest the
involvement of kinetic resolution and reductive elimination
in the catalytic cycle.
